title: Rodent EAE model for the study of axon integrity and remyelination
protocol: Dilute the MOG peptide in 0.01M phosphate buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) to a final concentration of 2 mg/ml.

Mix equal volumes of MOG/PBS and complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA, 2mg/ml) thoroughly between two 5-ml glass syringes using a three-way stopcock with a Luer connector to form a thick peptide/CFA emulsion.
Centrifuge the emulsion gently and load slowly into a 1-ml syringe using an 18 gauge needle.
Replace the 18 gauge needle with a 27 gauge needle for subcutaneous injection of 200 μl of MOG/CFA emulsion into two sites at flank, 100 μl per site.
Inject 50 ng (100 μl) of Bordetella pertussis toxin intraperitoneally.
Weigh each animal after MOG induction daily.
Determine EAE scores for motor functions daily.
Pay special attention to food, water, and urination once mice show clinical symptoms of EAE.
Euthanize the MOG-immunized mice 10 days later.
Remove and pool inguinal and axillary lymph nodes and spleen in DMEM.
Pass the tissues through a sterile cell strainer with 100 μm mesh attached to a sterile 1-ml syringe.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 1000 rpm for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in DMEM.
Lose the red blood cells with Gey’s hemolytic solution.
Incubate the mixture for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash the cell with DMEM.
Count the number of live cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 1000 rpm for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells at 5 x 10^6 cells/ml in DMEM containing 10% FCS, 20 μg/ml MOG 35-55 peptide and 20 ng/ml murine IL-12.
Keep the cells at 37°C, 10% CO2 for three days.
Wash the cells once with PBS before harvest.
Inject mouse intraperitoneally with 2.5-3 x 10^7 cells in 200 μl PBS and 50 ng pertussis toxin in 100 μl PBS.
Mix 50 μl of CFA with 50 μl of recombinant rat MOG in an eppendorf tube.
Anesthetize rats with a ketamine/xylazine mixture (80 mg/kg/8 mg/kg).
Inject the 100 μl cocktail into the base of the tail by intradermal injection.
Perform the injection slowly, requiring about 30-60 seconds before removing the needle.
Determine the EAE scores for each rat using a specified grading system.
Monitor rats for clinical symptoms of EAE beginning around 9 to 20 days post-immunization.
Kill rats if their body weight loss exceeds one-third of initial body weight or if they reach an EAE score of 3.5 or higher.
Pay special attention to food, water intake, and urination in rats showing signs of EAE.
Treat randomly assigned MOG-induced animals by intrathecal delivery of antagonist antibody to LINGO-1 or isotype control antibody (IgG) three days after MOG induction.
Anesthetize the rats and expose the vertebrae at lumbar level.
Drill a 1 mm hole on the fourth lumbar vertebra.
Insert the tip of the cannula connected with the pump into the hole for about 2 mm depth on the L4 vertebra and fix with instant glue.
At the end of the study, check the position of the pump's tip to ensure that it is in the subarachnoid space.
Check the residual volume in the pump to ensure the success of delivery.
Deliver the drug systemically after the onset of EAE clinical symptoms by intraperitoneal injections of 8 mg/kg antibody twice per week, commencing when an EAE score of 1 is reached.
Sacrifice the rats after two weeks of treatment.
Prepare fixative with 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1M phosphate buffer, pH7.4.
Stir and heat the fixative at 60°C for approximately 1.5 hours on a magnetic hotplate.
Filter the fixative before use.
Cool the fixative to 37°C or below.
Deeply anesthetize the animal with an overdose of pentobarbital (150 mg/kg).
Perfuse the rat with 50 ml of 0.9% normal saline solution intracardially.
Continue perfusing the rat with 250-300 ml of 4% paraformaldehyde solution intracardially.
Post-fix the tissues in the same fixative at 4°C for at least 4 hours.
Add a few drops of 1M sodium hydroxide solution to fully dissolve the paraformaldehyde and clear the solution.
After post fixation, dehydrate the tissue in 70% ethanol at room temperature overnight.
Remove the 70% ethanol and dehydrate the tissue in graded ethanol (80%, 95%, and 100%) at room temperature for total of 5 hours.
Clear the tissue with chloroform overnight at room temperature.
Embed tissues in melted paraffin wax at 56-58°C for 3 hours, with 3 changes of wax.
Maintain embedded blocks at 4°C until sectioning.
Cut 10 μm sections with a microtome and collect on a drop of distilled water on a gelatin-coated glass slide.
Dry the sections overnight at 37°C.
De-wax sections with toluene and graded ethanol (100% and 95%).
Stain sections in filtered 0.1% Luxol Fast Blue solution at 37°C overnight.
Wash stained sections in 70% ethanol followed by tap water.
Differentiate stained sections in 0.05% lithium carbonate solution and wash in tap water.
Counterstain with 1% neutral red solution for 5 minutes.
Dehydrate the sections in graded ethanol, clear in toluene, and mount with mounting medium.
Check sections under microscope until grey and white matters are distinguished.
Freshly prepare EM fixative (2.5% glutaraldehyde and 2% paraformaldehyde in 0.1M PB, pH7.4) before use.
Fix tissues at 4°C for 4 hours, then wash 3 times with 0.1M PB.
Post-fix the tissues in freshly prepared 1% osmium tetroxide at 4°C overnight, then wash 3 times with 0.1M PB.
Dehydrate the tissues in graded ethanol (30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 95%) for 5 minutes each followed by three changes in absolute ethanol for 10 minutes each.
Immerse the tissues in a 1:1 PO:Epon mixture for 1 hour, then overnight in pure Epon.
Embed the tissues in pure Epon and keep at 60°C for 3 days.
Mix MNA, DDSA, Taab 812 resin, DMP, and Poly cut-ease (12.5 ml, 15 ml, 22.5 ml, 0.9 ml, and 0.75 ml respectively) to prepare Epon.
Store the prepared Epon at -20°C and use at room temperature.
Cut 1 μm semi-thin sections from Epon-embedded tissue using a glass knife with an ultracut microtome.
Collect the sections on a drop of distilled water on a gelatin-coated glass slide.
Dry the collected sections on a hot plate at 80-100°C for 2 hours.
Prepare a staining solution of 0.5% toluidine blue in 1% sodium tetraborate.
Stain the sections on a hot plate at 80-100°C for 2 minutes.
Wash the stained sections with distilled water and dry them on a hot plate.
Dehydrate the sections in graded ethanol.
Clear the sections in toluene.
Mount the cleared sections with mounting medium.
Cut 90 nm sections from Epon embedded tissue using a diamond knife with an ultracut microtome and collect on a 200 mesh copper grid.
Prepare approximately 3% lead citrate before use.
Filter lead citrate before use.
Stain the grids with lead citrate droplets for 20 min in a Petri dish containing sodium hydroxide pellets to absorb carbon dioxide.
Wash the grids 3 times with distilled water after lead staining.
Prepare and filter 8% uranyl acetate before use.
Stain the sections on droplets of 8% uranyl acetate inside a Petri dish at room temperature for 20 min.
Wash the grids 3 times with distilled water after uranyl acetate staining.
Sections are now ready for electron microscopic analysis.
Trace the total cross-sectional area and demyelination area of each section with Image J software.
Express the demyelination as a percentage of the total demyelination area over total spinal cord area using random sections from L4 of each animal.
Sample axons intercepted by nine fixed sampling lines in toluidine blue stained semithin sections of L4 spinal segment.
Select nine tissue strips extending from the gray matter to the pial surface under the 100X oil-immersion objective of a light microscope.
Count all myelinated axons whose axoplasm was intercepted by the sampling line.
Pool the axonal profiles from the tissue strips of each rat.
Immerse the spinal cord into a plastic tube filled with 4% paraformaldehyde after fixation.
Suspend the spinal cord in formalin solution before and during MRI scan.
Acquire diffusion-weighted spin echo imaging sequence using a rotationally invariant icosahedral encoding scheme with 6 encoding directions.

Set imaging parameters to TR/TE = 1600/29.0 ms, δ/Δ=3/20 ms, slice thickness = 2 mm (interslice gap = 0.2 mm), FOV = 27 mm, data matrix = 256 x 256 (zero filled to 512 x 512), image resolution = 105 x 105 μm² and two b-values as 0 and 1000 s/mm².
Repeat the sequence 3 times for signal averaging.
Extract diffusion tensors \(DTs) using an in-house Matlab program interfaced with a software implementing the constrained nonlinear least squares methods for eigenvalue estimation.
Diagonalize the extracted diffusion tensors to estimate three diffusion eigenvalues, \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\), and \(\lambda_3\).
Measure mean diffusivity in the ventral, dorsal, left lateral, and right lateral column of the second and third segment of the spinal cord.
Measure axial diffusivity in the ventral, dorsal, left lateral, and right lateral column of the second and third segment of the spinal cord.
Measure radial diffusivity in the ventral, dorsal, left lateral, and right lateral column of the second and third segment of the spinal cord.
Measure fractional anisotropy in the ventral, dorsal, left lateral, and right lateral column of the second and third segment of the spinal cord.
Draw regions of interest based on \(\lambda\), T2-weighted images to avoid covering gray matter.
